Class TreeGridModel<T>

java.lang.Object
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model.AbstractGridModel
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model.TreeGridModel<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of the items
All Implemented Interfaces:
GridModel
public class TreeGridModel<T> extends AbstractGridModel

A tree of items shown as rows: every item is a row, and the children of an expanded item follow it. Show it in a TreeGrid, which indents the first column and adds the triangles that expand and collapse.

TreeGridModel<Unit> company = new TreeGridModel<Unit>(Unit::children)
        .column("Name", Unit::name)
        .column("People", Unit::people);
company.setRoots(List.of(headquarters));
Grid grid = new TreeGrid(company);
  • Expanding inserts the rows of the children and collapsing deletes them, so a grid keeps its selection and its scroll position as with any other change.
  • The children function is called when an item is first expanded or shown with its triangle, so a large tree can be loaded as it is opened.
  • Each item in the tree is expanded on its own. setRoots(Collection) keeps items expanded that equal (equals) items expanded before.
  • Sorting sorts the children of each item, so the tree stays a tree.
  • setRoots(Collection) and the builders may be called from any thread, see AbstractGridModel.applyChange(Runnable). Reading methods and setExpanded(int, boolean) belong to the JavaFX application thread, where row numbers are current.

      public void setExpanded(int row, boolean expand)
      Shows or hides the children of the item in a row. Expanding inserts the rows of its children, and of theirs where those are expanded; collapsing deletes them and keeps which of them are expanded.
      Parameters:

      expand - whether to show its children

    • sortRows

      public boolean sortRows(List<SortKey> keys, IntFunction<Comparator<Object>> order)
      Sorts the children of each item, and the top-level items, by the keys in the order the grid passes; no keys bring back the order of the children function.
      Parameters:
      keys - the columns to sort by, the first one decides and the next ones break its ties; empty for the model's natural order
      order - the order of a model column's values, ascending, nulls first: the column's comparator or the grid's default order (numbers by value, text ignoring case). Models that sort somewhere else, such as in a database, can ignore it.
      Returns:
      true if the model sorted its rows
